Pattern: CONTRADICTION_REVEAL_V4. Audience: global English-speaking viewers; state country, model and time scope naturally. Channel angle: familiar things with an unexpected design or function. Generate five declarative, concrete subject-first hooks; prefer 6–10 words, max 12 only for a justified exception. Six story functions across five voiced scenes: visual paradox, contradiction, clue, mechanism, distinct second reveal, payoff. Target 25–29 seconds including the configured sign-off; hard max 30. Keep spoken/display copy, voice, karaoke, local BGM and channel outro. No generic CTA. For every voiced scene, make a distinct Gemini portrait still and Google Flow six-second animation using the same Tell character. Review visible action, 9:16 crop and continuity before binding local MP4s. Generated scenes explain sourced facts; they are not documentary proof. No added on-screen captions or labels, logos, dark wash, or photoreal footage; preserve factual numbers and markings on the object.
Packaging claim: Lightning and Thunder Start Together
Core fact: The National Weather Service says thunder is the sound generated by lightning.
Second reveal: Light reaches observers faster than sound, so the flash is seen before the thunder is heard.
First frame: show one lightning flash and a delayed sound wave immediately, large and recognizable. Animate the physical change or causal chain without invented labels or unsupported details. Tell points or reacts without covering the object.
Fact boundaries: If thunder is audible, seek shelter; do not use a seconds count as a safety clearance.
